title: Funding for places
amount_raw: Minimum grant £15,000–£100,000 and usual grant range spanning £15,000 up to £1 million depending on sector/stream
eligibility_summary: UK-based organisations (registered/exempt charities, local authorities, universities and research institutions) applying for capital projects. The twelve applying sector categories are grouped by the funder into three streams shown in each page's 'Wolfson funding programme' field: Health & Disability (charities working with disability / mental health / older people; hospices & palliative care; special needs schools & colleges); Heritage, Humanities & the Arts (historic buildings & landscapes; libraries & archives; museums & galleries; performing arts); Science & Medicine (public engagement with science; universities & research institutions). Projects must be capital (new build, refurbishment or equipment); most sectors require project cost of at least £50,000 with a funding shortfall of at least £25,000 (heritage sectors have a £15,000 floor). Match funding (typically 25% for larger projects) and any planning permission must be in place by the invitation-only Stage 2. Five-year wait before reapplying.
summary: Wolfson's main capital grants programme (about 85% of its funding). Two-stage: a short online Stage 1 form submitted within defined annual windows, then an invitation-only Stage 2. Funds buildings (new build or refurbishment) and equipment across education, science & medicine, health & disability, and heritage, humanities & the arts.
notes: SUPERSEDES existing row wolfson-funding-for-places (which was labelled off the landing page before the sector detail pages were captured). DISTINCT-VS-ONE-PROGRAMME DECISION: the thirteen linked sector pages are sector-specific eligibility guidance for ONE capital programme, not thirteen distinct calls, so they are represented as this single row plus one separate row for the genuinely distinct secondary-education call. Evidence: eleven of the sector pages (charities-mental-health, charities-disability, charities-older-people, historic-buildings-landscapes, hospices-palliative-care, libraries-archives, museums-galleries, performing-arts, public-engagement-with-science, universities-research-institutions, special-schools-and-colleges) each state the IDENTICAL two-stage process and the IDENTICAL recurring deadline calendar (Round 1: Stage 1 opens 20 November, Stage 1 deadline 5 January, Stage 2 deadline 1 March, decision June; Round 2: Stage 1 opens 14 May, Stage 1 deadline 1 July, Stage 2 deadline 1 September, decision December); all share one online (Blackbaud) application system. The funding-for-places/start-your-application page confirms the funder itself collapses the sectors into just three application entry points (Science & Medicine; Health & Disability; Heritage, Humanities & the Arts). The places-of-worship page is a signpost only (routes applicants to the National Churches Trust Wolfson Fabric Repair Grants and to the historic-buildings programme) and is not itself a call. What varies by sector is only the grant range and eligibility, i.e. parameter/eligibility variants of one programme. STATUS CORRECTION: the old row called this open/rolling from FAQ wording; the detail pages show Stage 1 is WINDOWED (Round 2 Stage 1 window 14 May–1 July had closed by the 2026-08-16 snapshot; next Stage 1 window opens 20 November), so a new applicant cannot submit on the snapshot date -> status=forthcoming, next_open_date=2026-11-20. Stage 2 is invitation-only (restricted). Recorded deadlines are the next occurrences of the four recurring submission deadlines (Stage 2 1 Sep 2026; Stage 1 5 Jan 2027; Stage 2 1 Mar 2027; Stage 1 1 Jul 2027) — no year is printed on the pages, hence deadlines/next_open_date flagged uncertain. PER-SECTOR USUAL GRANT RANGES for a reviewer who prefers to split into three stream rows: Health & Disability sectors mostly £40,000–£75,000 (hospices £50,000–£150,000), min grant £25,000; Heritage/Humanities/Arts £15,000–£100,000 (museums £50,000–£500,000; performing arts £50,000–£150,000), min grant £15,000; Science & Medicine £250,000–£1,000,000 (public engagement with science £250,000–£750,000; universities £250,000–£1m), min grant £100,000. amount_min/max here span the full programme (15000 to 1000000). FLAG FOR REVIEW: splitting places into three stream rows is a defensible alternative, but the streams share one identical deadline calendar and amount varies by sector within a stream, so a single programme row is the cleaner canonical unit. UMBRELLA-ROW UPDATE 2026-08-23: the eleven sector pages listed in this note as evidence are now labelled as distinct in-scope opportunities in their own right (wolfson-charities-working-in-mental-health, wolfson-charities-working-with-disability, wolfson-charities-working-with-older-people, wolfson-historic-buildings-landscapes, wolfson-hospices-and-palliative-care-organisations, wolfson-libraries-archives, wolfson-museums-galleries, wolfson-performing-arts-organisations, wolfson-public-engagement-with-science-organisations, wolfson-special-schools-and-colleges, wolfson-universities-and-research-institutions), each carrying its own grant range and eligibility. This row is retained as the programme-level/umbrella entry and remains in scope. A scorer counting both this row and the eleven sector rows as separate hits is counting one capital programme twice, so decide explicitly whether recall is measured against the umbrella row, the sector rows, or both. wolfson-places-of-worship remains out of scope as a signpost with no call of its own.

title: Funding for secondary schools & sixth form colleges
amount_raw: Minimum £15,000, maximum £100,000; usual grant range £15,000–£50,000 (equipment) and £15,000–£100,000 (new build and refurbishment)
eligibility_summary: State-funded secondary schools and sixth form colleges (MATs apply on behalf of member schools, one application per MAT per round) with at least two years of exam results and a 'Good'-or-above inspection outcome. Special schools are excluded and directed to the special needs schools & colleges programme.

exclusion_reason: Fails the inclusion rule: on the 2026-08-16 snapshot the page states 'Our 2026 funding round is now closed' and only that the Foundation 'expect[s] to share the dates and details of our next funding round in spring 2027' — an announcement date, not a stated future OPEN date. notes: SUPERSEDES existing row wolfson-secondary-education-programme (which was labelled off the application-guidance page and inferred status=open/in_scope=yes on thin evidence). The now-captured detail page shows this is a genuinely DISTINCT call from the main two-stage places programme: it uses a ONE-stage process, has its own timing, and its own grant band (£15,000–£100,000). CORRECTION: the old row guessed open; the page in fact says the 2026 round is CLOSED (decisions November 2026) with next-round details only 'expected in spring 2027', so it is excluded (parallel to the Leverhulme major-research-fellowships case: future information but no stated future opening). next_open_date flagged uncertain because 'spring 2027' is when details will be shared, not a confirmed opening date. Distinct from special schools & colleges, which share the two-stage places calendar and are covered by the programme row.
